in_text_mentions: e (Figure 1). Other remarkable imaging findings included scrotal wall thickening and diffusely distorted parenchymal echotexture, especially at the proximal pole of the testis. The hyperechoic linear border of the testis indicative of the tunica albuginea was breached in the setting of a testicular tear (Figure 2). A few scattered, focal, hyperechoic, intraparenchymal areas represented small intratesticular hematomas (Figure 3). On color Doppler exam, a large echogenic area was revealed at the upper pole of the testis lacking vascularity (Figure 4). There was no evidence of testicular torsion.

panels.rationale: Single ultrasound panel from a case of blunt scrotal trauma showing a testicular fracture line, heterogeneous parenchyma, and hematocele, directly supporting testicular rupture.
panels.attribution_text: Blok et al. Testicular Rupture Following Blunt Scrotal Trauma.. Case reports in emergency medicine 2019. doi:10.1155/2019/7058728. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Left testicle sagittal plane. There is abnormal tunica albuginea thickening ([) without obvious disruption, a moderate-sized hematocele (∗), and a linear hypoechoic fracture line (between white arrows) separating a heterogenous appearing testicular parenchyma. Normal testicular parenchyma is present to the left with an abnormal appearance testicle to the right of the fracture line, consistent with an intratesticular contusion.
in_text_mentions: Scrotal ultrasonography was performed by the emergency physician at the bedside. This showed moderate scrotal edema on the left with testicular contusion and hematocele. Thickening of the tunica albuginea and subtle contour deformity were consistent with left testicular fracture (Figures 1 and 2). There was no evidence of torsion or infarction.

panels.figure_caption: Sagittal grayscale ultrasound of the right testicle approximately 18 hours after injury. Exam shows contour irregularity and tunica albuginea disruption (red arrow), hematoma collection (blue arrow), and heterogenous echotexture. in_text_mentions: e right tunica albuginea with eccentric echogenicity of the right testicular body and a heterogenous, avascular collection, compatible with right testicular rupture and an associated hematoma (Figure 1, 2). The urology team opted for non-operative management of the scrotal trauma due to a nearly 18-hour delay in diagnosis of the testicular injury. panels.rationale: Single-panel ultrasound image labeled RT. TESTIS showing a fractured right testicle. The caption and in-text describe irregular hypoechoic regions in the lower pole of the right testis and suggest right testicular fracture, supporting a testicular rupture–spectrum manifestation with a fracture line and heterogeneous parenchyma. The tunica albuginea is described as intact, so no tunica disruption finding is assigned. [raw subtype: testicular_fracture]
panels.attribution_text: Addas et al. Testicular Rupture or Testicular Fracture? A Case Report and Literature Review.. Case reports in urology 2018. doi:10.1155/2018/1323780. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Fractured right testicle on ultrasound scan.
in_text_mentions: Scrotal ultrasonography showed irregular hypoechoic regions in the lower pole of the right testis with no significant Doppler flow evident. The tunica albuginea appeared intact and there was slightly increased Doppler flow in the rest of the testis. The left testis was normal. (Figures 1 and 2). The ultrasound scan findings suggested a right testicular fracture to be the most likely pathology but rupture could not be excluded or confirmed. Both testes appeared normal in size.

findings.label: Heterogeneous testicular parenchyma
findings.evidence: heterogeneous and avascular echotexture of the upper pole of the right testis

panels.rationale: Single-panel color Doppler ultrasound of the right testis from an article on testicular rupture in an adolescent; the caption explicitly describes a heterogeneous, avascular echotexture of the upper pole of the right testis in the setting of a larger testicular hematoma contusion, matching the vocabulary finding of heterogeneous testicular parenchyma in testicular rupture. Real patient sonographic image with no third-party copyright indication.
panels.attribution_text: Papathanassiou et al. Testicular Rupture: Clinical, Sonographic, and Surgical Correlation in an Adolescent Patient.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.78688. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Testicular heterogeneity. The sagittal ultrasound color Doppler plane demonstrated a heterogeneous and avascular echotexture of the upper pole of the right testis in the setting of a larger testicular hematoma contusion.

findings.label: Disrupted tunica albuginea on ultrasound
findings.evidence: Prolapse of ruptured tunica albuginea (arrow); MRI indicated ... partial disruption of the tunica albuginea

panels.rationale: Single MRI panel from a patient with suspected testicular rupture; caption explicitly shows prolapse of ruptured tunica albuginea and testicular contents, directly supporting the configured disease.
panels.attribution_text: Yokokawa et al. Testicular rupture successfully treated with a tunica vaginalis flap.. IJU case reports 2021. doi:10.1002/iju5.12246. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Prolapse of ruptured tunica albuginea (arrow) and testicular contents (arrowhead).
in_text_mentions: cluding a swollen testis with heterogeneous echogenicity. Doppler ultrasonography revealed no blood flow in the left testis. Blood flow was maintained in the right scrotum, and both epididymides were normal (Fig. 1). MRI indicated swelling of the left testis with surrounding high‐intensity areas and partial disruption of the tunica albuginea (Fig. 2). The preoperative levels of LH, FSH, and testosterone were 6.7 mIU/mL, 13.8 mIU/mL, and 1065.9 ng/dL, respectively. Thus, we suspected testicular rupture with damage to the tunica albuginea. Emergency surgery was performed on the day of admission.
